chapter: Probation, Las Vegas and Los Angeles in the 1950s
title: Other gigs: Phineas Newborn in San Diego, the Rowles trio, the Clef Club
summary: Short jobs including a trio with Jimmy Rowles and Irv Cottler and a week with Eddie Shu and Lenny Bruce.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: After you worked with Rex here where did you play next?
Long and in between I played the Soho down in San Diego with Phineas Newborn, for five days.
The Soho. Was that what you said?
Yeah. And then I came back here and I had a few one nighters with Jimmy Rowles.
Then -- yeah, during this period, because, see, in '53, Jimmy Rowles and Irv Cottler and I had a trio together,

over on La Cienega, just before you get to Hollywood Boulevard there's a club over there, and Jack Palance used to sit in a booth every night, (Unintelligible), and we kept the place packed all the time. We were playing all of Count Basie's tunes, you know, "Jiving at Five", and --
What was the name of that? I don't remember that.

I can't remember the name of the club. I think it was the Celebrity Club. But when I came back out here, and I was getting these one nighters and things, the Clef Club was open at that time. And I went in there and I worked I guess about a week, with Eddie Shu , and Art Blakey had just closed, and Eddie Shu followed him in, playing the saxophone and harmonica, and Lenny Bruce was on the bill, so I met him. And later Kenny Drew, the pianist, took me out to his house, and I met his wife, and they had a newborn baby, and they appeared to be very happy, you know. Then time went by, and I found out what was happening.
Yeah. She and my daughter went to school together.
She should be older than that. '53?
Well, my daughter was born in '55 and she and Kitty are the same age. They went to school together.
'55. Oh, I was still out here, because I stayed out here from '53 to '56, till my probation was up.
